key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation leads to different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap control must be tailored to the specific absorber chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This work enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells with tunable bandgaps and demonstrates a practical path to higher-efficiency, scalable tandem manufacturing.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compared conversion in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Used the insights to design tandem absorbers spanning 1.26–1.96 eV
evidence_signal: The study reports a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell reaching 19.2% efficiency and 80% average retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and incomplete interdiffusion in the NBG stack may complicate reproducibility and long-term stability in scaled devices.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
